title: "Robust Correlation"
format: html
editor: visual

## We generate some toy data to show different ways to compute correlation:

```{r}
xx <-runif(n = 1000,min=0,max=1)
yy <-xx^2 + rnorm(n=1000,sd=0.1)
yy[800:1000]<--4*xx[800:1000]^6

plot(xx,yy)
```

### Pearson Correlation

```{r}
cor1<-cor(xx,yy)
print(cor1)
```

However, we can use some other robust methods against outliers:

### Spearman Correlation

-   more robust to outliers than Pearson

-   If you don't have outliers and have a normally distributed data, you don't need to use Spearman.

-   measures by ranks of data for correlation

```{r}
cor(xx,yy, method = "spearman")
```

### Robust Correlation from Robust Covariance Matrix

The best method when you have outliers

```{r}
library(MASS)
ccs<-cov.rob(data.frame(xx,yy))
cor2<-cov2cor(ccs$cov)[1,2]
print(cor2)
```

```{r}
plot(xx,yy)
points(xx,cor1*xx,col="red")# pearson
points(xx,cor2*xx,col="blue")# robust 
```

The part trending down is all outliers.
